text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up re: model weight loading. I want to push a concrete "merge-path streaming" design for safetensors + sharded bundles. Goal: allow model READY once critical tensors are present, stream remaining pieces, verify checksums, and enable early warmup of attention kernels.

jen: short question 1: how do we pick "critical" tensors? we need a deterministic rule for all models.

maria: rule proposal: critical set = {input embeddings, final ln weights, kvmeta, first 2 layer weights}. heuristic can be model-profile driven (per-arch defaults) and overridable in manifest.

jahir: sketch the on-disk layout pls. manifest? per-shard headers? i want to see failure modes.

maria: layout: top-level manifest.json (signed) + shards. manifest lists shards and a per-tensor index mapping tensor_name -> [(shard, offset, length, piece_idx)]. each shard begins with small header: {shard_id, piece_count, piece_checksums:[...]} so we can verify each piece as it arrives. example manifest snippet in-thread: ```json
{"model":"redwood/gpt-lite","shards":["gpt-000.safetensors","gpt-001.safetensors"],"shard_strategy":"merge-path","critical_tensors":["tok_embeddings","ln_f.weight","kv_meta"]}```

tom: Piece-level checksums + signature is good. Tradeoffs: more metadata increases manifest size but lets us stream safely. Also: need atomic swap for Dedicated/Private.

maria: atomic swap flow: 1) download manifest + manifest.sig 2) verify sig (KMS-verified) 3) begin async fetch of critical pieces 4) verify pieces against checksums 5) if critical set ok -> mark model READY and swap pointer 6) continue background fetch of rest. If sig or checksums fail, keep previous manifest and emit alert. infra-bot: deploy-checklist: manifest.sig verified, critical pieces verified, no CRC errors.

jen: warmup strategy? naive token warmup will hammer IO.

maria: Priority-based async warmup: we rank tensors by (role_priority, size, layer_index). role_priority: embedding/kvmeta/first_layers/KV_cache. warmup proceeds until either critical memory budget or time budget is hit. non-critical tensors fetched lazily. early-completion path: runtime can generate short replies using partial model (first N layers) while later layers stream in.

tom: Loader API sketch (keeps runtime decoupled): ```py
class Loader:
    async def fetch_piece(self, shard: str, piece_idx: int) -> bytes: ...
    async def prefetch_tensors(self, tensor_names: list[str]) -> None: ...
    def mmap_backing(self, path: str) -> Optional[memoryview]: ...
    def close(self): ...
```
Runtime asks for flavor: direct_map vs decode_stream.

jahir: mmap + quantized formats? we need two access flavors.

maria: Exactly. Support direct_map (mmapped, read-only memoryview) for raw float/uint8 aligned tensors. For quantized/compressed tensors we expose decode_stream: async generator yielding decompressed chunks so the runtime can decode in-place or stream to GPU. runtime chooses based on tensor profile in manifest (quantization tag).

jen: eviction + cache: pieces can live on local NVMe cache or remote S3. need eviction policy.

maria: propose LRU-weighted by size and recent access frequency, with hard cap on decompressed RAM and soft cap on on-disk cache. also support explicit pin lists for hot models.

jahir: how to handle in-flight generation when a tensor piece is missing? blocking would be bad.

maria: KV-cache strategy: allocate zero-pages placeholders for missing pages. runtime continues; when piece arrives we patch pages in-place and re-run dependent attention windows if needed. For model weights used in forward passes we try to ensure critical forward paths are present; otherwise fall back to a degraded fast path (e.g., smaller model variant or cached logits).

tom: error cases: partial piece corruption, mid-download failure, manifest drift. Need deterministic recovery.

maria: recovery rules: - piece checksum mismatch -> mark piece corrupt, re-fetch up to N retries from other mirrors - repeated failures -> mark shard unhealthy and fall back to compatible model variant (manifest contains fallback_model). - manifest signature mismatch -> abort swap and keep previous model. emit metrics and alert.

jen: perf: any numbers? streaming helps startup latency but increases steady-state IO.

maria: rough expectations from lab tests: full-download cold start: 18s for 13B over 10GbE. merge-path critical-only READY in ~2.2s (embeddings+first 2 layers). steady-state token throughput unaffected once all pieces present; background fetch bandwidth ~20-40MB/s depending on disk. will measure more.

jahir: testing plan? need deterministic unit tests + integration tests with flaky networks.

maria: tests: (1) unit: piece verify, manifest parsing, mmap vs decode flavors (2) integration: simulated flaky S3 (latency, stalls, checksum corruption) + assert READY invariants (only ready after critical pieces) (3) perf harness: compare cold-start latencies and memory graphs. open TODO: add model profile generator to compute critical set per-arch automatically.

tom: who owns the loader and runtime interface? we need clear ownership to avoid API churn.

maria: propose eng-runtime owns Loader interface; eng-ml owns manifest schema & shard strategy definitions; eng-infra owns signing/manifest distribution. create cross-team RFC doc and a 2-week spike (maria + tom + infra-engineer) to implement prototype.

jen: ack. can we add a simple fallback flag in manifest to prefer mmap if available? helps on-prem.

maria: yes: manifest field 'preferred_access': {"tensor_name": "mmap|stream"}. runtime uses this hint but loader can override if backend doesn't support mmap.

infra-bot: action items created: #deploy-mergepath-spike, #manifest-signing-policy, #loader-api-rfc.

jen: thanks, this seems actionable. next step: repo spike + minimal prototype that serves a toy 2-shard model and validates warmup/READY flow.

maria: I'll open the spike PR and link the test harness. will post timeline in #eng-ml tomorrow. :rocket:
